purpose: ONE timing decision for an OFP station notice. The app (dashboard chart, PDF map marks, NOTAM records) and ODSS (airport cards, PDF consequences, PDF cards) each read the same LIDO record from the same OFP; both evaluate it with these rules, byte-identical in both repos (app notam-timing-rules.json = ODSS app/odss/notam_timing_rules.json), and both suites run tests/fixtures/notam-timing-vectors.json. Item 3 (Gatwick, 14 Oct 2026): the decision was made by three evaluators with three rule sets.

stationWindows.readFrom: Operator default: NOTAM validity is assessed two hours either side of the station time (app 94a7019, 25 Jul 2026; HelpYou plan A8, 30 Jul 2026: 'window default +/-2h stays'). ODSS had kept a one-hour departure window, so a closure 60-120 min from ETD was drawn on the chart and the PDF map but absent from the card and the PDF text.

noReferenceStations.note: Destination alternates, EDTO, fuel-enroute and enroute stations: the app holds no reference instant (window ETA-2h to ETA+24h, boss 02 Sep chart ruling); ODSS judges alternates at the destination ETA (ETA +/-2h), EDTO at sector entry, fuel-enroute and enroute at departure. That policy is the product owner's to choose; until then each runtime keeps its own window and reference for those roles. The evaluation rules below are shared for every role.

rules: The LIDO VALID range is start ' - ' end. No start, or no end that reads as a date-time, UFN or PERM, is a timing review: an absent end is never read as open-ended.
UFN and PERM are open-ended: in force from the start, no end is invented.
An EST end is held as the end (flagged estimated), as both runtimes did before this spec.
Start is inclusive and end is exclusive.

benign.note: A radio frequency, by its band and decimals or its unit: 118.100, 121.9MHZ, 335 KHZ; an NDB's kHz after NDB and its ident: NDB 'RIC' 347; a DME/TACAN channel after its frequency or CH: 115.3/100X, CH 79X.
A telephone number after TEL/PHONE/FAX/FOR INFO, or written with a leading + (+65 6123 4567).
A telephone number in a fixed national format, whole (with an AT before it): 617-561-1919, (866) 598-9522, 07484 424457, 03-3268-3111, 02 6128 4339, 0411 253 135.
A number (or a number range or list of sectors) with its unit: 1800-2000FT AMSL, 2400 M, 210 KNOTS, 3 DEG, 180-DEGREE, 15.00 DME, 841 MSL, 1 700 M (thousands spaced), 190-205 DEG.
A number of seconds, or a range of them, with the unit: 300 SEC (an interval) - never holding a clock-like range.
A number of minutes, or a range of them, with the unit: 30 MIN, 15 AND 30 MINUTES (minutes are intervals, never periods).
A flight level or a flight-level band: FL110, FL 245-460, 470FL/660FL.
A route or sector altitude (MOCA, MSA, MEA, MORA ...), its segment or up to three named points first - never a weekday, month or period word: 'MOCA FROM CUTOX TO CUJKE 1200 TO 1900'.

benign.note: A document number after its keyword (NOTAM, SUP, SUPPLEMENT, AIC, AMDT, BULLETIN, REF, BFS ...) and any series letters, with its year: 'AIP SUP 192/2025', 'AIC M 076/2026', 'AMDT 04/26', 'FDC NOTAM 0-9801', 'MOWP 2024-1' - never a bare number pair, which may be clocks or a date.
An FAA obstruction case number, by its year and region: 2025-AEA-4238-NRA, 2023-AEA-2063 THRU 2068-NRA, 2024-15030/31-NRA.
An aeronautical-study or permission case number: 34-082748, AR-2026-4066/08, TS-013-26/TC-1.
A document's date after DATED/ISSUED/PUBLISHED/SIGNED, or glued after an AIP page number: 'REF CHART DATED 20 MAR 2025', 'AD 2.4-5/17 APR 2025'.
MAY the verb, by the verb after it - after a number or a sign a verb, never an adverb (ONLY, ALSO ...), so '01 MAY ONLY' stays a date: 'ACFT MAY BE', 'RWY 27 MAY BE SLIPPERY', 'U/S, MAY TRANSMIT'.
The sun itself: 'REFLECTION OF THE SUN', 'SUN GLARE', 'SUN REFLECTIONS' - never after a restriction verb, a time preposition or a weekday joiner.

Obstacle and work-area marking or lighting by day or night: 'DAY AND NIGHT MARKED', 'WILL BE LIGHTED AT NIGHT', 'MARKED AND LGTD AT NGT' - lighting only in the passive (an obstacle that is lit), never after a restriction verb.
A place name containing a period word (HO).

benign.note: A notice, permission or restoration lead time, ONLY in its explicit context: 'PPR 48 HOURS', 'PRIOR PERMISSION AT LEAST 1HR BFR', '24 HR PN', '60 MIN NOTIFICATION', 'RE-OPN WI 2 HR', 'AVBL WI 2 HR', 'MAX RESTORATION TIME 04HRS', 'WI 24 HR FM OCCURRENCE', 'FPLS AT LEAST 3 HR BFR THE EOBT' (an application lead time), 'NOTIFY ATC 24 HR IN ADVANCE'. A duration attached to the restriction itself - FOR, MAX, LAST, PERIOD OF, DURING, UP TO, WI alone - is temporal content.

The hours of an office, masked ONLY inside a contact sentence: the sentence holds a contact or communication verb (CONTACT, CTC, CALL, TEL, REQUEST, APPLY, NOTIFY, OBTAIN, ARRANGE, COORDINATE ...) and no restriction verb (CLSD, U/S, AVBL, OPR, ACT, RESTRICTED ...); only the hours phrase is masked (maskGroup 1): 'TWY J CLSD. CONTACT CAA DURING NORMAL OFFICE HOURS.', 'AFTER HOURS CTC TEL ...'. 'CLSD DURING THE OFFICE HOURS OF THE CAA' and 'CLSD, CONTACT ... OFFICE HOURS' are the restriction's own hours: temporal.

A document's own date: a NOTAM incorporated in an AIP amendment or SUP on a date, a chart's edition date ('FALE ILS-02 02 OCTOBER 2025'), a navigation database date, a bulletin issued on a date. A NOTAM superseded or replaced from a date is the notice's own end: temporal.

An identifier, not a time: an obstacle or crane reference number, a volcano or SATVOICE code, a hyphenated document ID ('APAM-1620-AF-BRF-0032'), a standard (DO-260B, 1090ES), an FAA GPS test (GPS 26-03), a stand label before its coordinates, an elevation between latitude and longitude, NOTAM item F) or G) limits.

A position: a latitude with its longitude ('1315N 12341E', '403901N0734653W', '372901.9896N / 1263136.8580E'), a latitude or longitude alone in seconds ('143248.67N', '1205929.43E') or in degrees, minutes and seconds (37DEG26'15.0000"N), or a parallel or meridian after WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH OF ('WEST OF 165W').
A magnetic variation and its epoch year: 'MAG VAR 1.75DEG W (2010)', 'VARIATION UPDATED TO 6DEG E 2025' - only the value between.
The year in an event's name, by the name after it: 'FOR 2026 FORMULA 1 SINGAPORE GRAND PRIX' - never after a time preposition, never with one between.
When a runway condition was observed (FICON): 'OBS AT 2607211210' - an observation, not a period.

A list or section label: one or two digits (with dotted sub-numbers) closed by '.', ')' or '-', or in brackets, or a dotted section number, or one digit alone opening a sentence, directly before a word of letters that is not a time unit, temporal connective, month, weekday, period or day word, number word or unit: '3. IF', '1.TFC', '(1) APPLY', '2) TWY', '3.2.1 LOCATION', '32-AWY' - never holding a clock-like shape (8.30).

A letter-led designator - a route, fix, waypoint, area, runway or chart identifier - and its hyphen or slash compound: Q907, RWY13R, LRTRA71L, SZ051, N/UN644, LEMOD-N644-DOBAT, RWY18R/36L, D3.3SHK, ARR-09, ZGSZ-5L-11:IAC - never with a time, period, day, month, weekday or connective prefix (H24, SR0600, TO1000), never letters standing for digits (O800), never one letter and four digits (L0800), never a time suffix (Q800Z).
A runway end alone, 01-36 with L, R or C: '16L', '03R', 'RWY END 34R/16L' (a time is never two digits and L).

A visibility in statute miles after VIS/VISIBILITY and its categories: 'VISIBILITY ALL CATS 1 3/8', 'VIS CAT C/D 1 1/4', 'VISIBILITY CAT C 2, CAT D 2 1/4' - a whole mile and a fraction in halves, quarters, eighths or sixteenths.
A runway condition code triple after FICON/RWYCC: 'FICON 5/5/5'.

A small number labelling the noun before it: 'TERMINAL 7', 'COLUMN 12', 'ALERT LVL 2', 'RFF CAT 8', 'AD 2', 'ISONE 1 ACT', 'MAP 13-2-1', 'PAD 2 AND 4' - the governing word a noun (never a temporal connective, a restriction or contact verb, a time, period or day word, a month, a weekday, a number word, a unit or a function word), never holding a temporal token, never followed by a time unit, temporal word or range.

A small number (or an ordinal) counting the noun after it: '3 BOATS', '2 LGT U/S', '1 CRANE ERECTED', '611TH BLDG' - the noun never a time unit, temporal word, verb or function word; never the object of a temporal connective or restriction verb.

An FAA location identifier of digit, letter, digit ('2A9', '6A8', '3Y2' - never H, L or Z between, the separators of a malformed clock: 8H3, 4L1, 0Z1), or one or two digits and one letter that is never a time letter (A/P for AM/PM, D, H, M, S, W, Y, Z for days, hours, minutes, seconds, weeks, years, Zulu; O and I stand for digits; L stays a runway end): '5G', '5J', '15X', '9V'.
A DME distance with its station ident and the unit DME ('FIX AT 3.2 ISW DME'), or a DME fix with its station in brackets ('4D(IAMR)', '11D(IAR)').

rules: Item D is printed as the first body line(s) of a LIDO record. Typographic hyphens and dashes (dashes) are read as '-'. The field is the leading run of body lines made only of schedule tokens (fieldLine), joined with one space: a D field wrapped over several lines is one field, wherever the line breaks ('AUG 16' then '1800-2000', 'AUG' then '16 1800-2000', 'AUG 16 1800-' then '2000').

The field is accepted only when the grammar below reads all of it. A leading run it cannot read in full - a date with no time, a clock written HH:MM (colonClock), '/' between two times, 2400, a zero-length range, an impossible date - is a timing review, never 'no schedule'.
Daylight, exception and holiday rules (reviewLanguage) are a timing review.

QA510 (fail closed). TEMPORAL CONTENT in the free text after the field is found by SHAPE, never by validity (temporal, every class named): any clock-LIKE shape whatever its values - 3 or 4 digits alone or with suffix letters (2500, 0860, 0800A, 0800GMT, 1800Z), 1 or 2 digits with a dot, colon, space or H and 2 more (08.00, 8:00, 08:00:00, 18 00, 18H00), 1 or 2 digits with an H (18H), a letter for a digit (080O, O800, 1O00; a lower-case l in a run holding a digit is first written I (letterForDigit), while an upper-case route designator such as L888 stays a designator; each line is first stripped of format characters and NFKC-normalised (normalisation), so a full-width or styled digit is a digit and no zero-width character splits a clock), 6 PM, 6 P.M., SIX O'CLOCK, and any of these, or a 2-digit number, on either side of a range connector (-, /, TO, TIL, TILL, UNTIL, THRU, THROUGH, AND: 0860-1060, 18-20, 0800-10, FROM 8 TO 10); a date-time group (6, 8 or 10 digits); any date or month form (01/09/2026, 01-09-26 ...); any weekday or day word (DAILY, DLY, WEEKDAYS, WEEKENDS, HOL, HOLIDAYS, DAYS, WEEK, MONTH ...); any period or daylight word (H24, HJ, HN, HX, HO, SR, SS, SUNRISE, SUNSET, DAYLIGHT, DARKNESS, NIGHT, NGT, EVENING, MORNING, AFTERNOON, DAWN, DUSK, MIDNIGHT, SUMMER, WINTER, SEASON, 24 HR); a reference to hours (HR, HOURS); a duration of an hour or longer (2 HR, 3 DAYS, SIX MONTHS - minutes are intervals, not periods); a UTC offset, or a time zone after a clock; an ordinal day (FIRST MONDAY, EVERY OTHER DAY); an activation reference (AUP, UUP, WHEN ACTIVATED). The grammar reads a clock only in its own forms (HHMM, HHMM with UTC or Z, a valid HHMM-HHMM range); any other clock-like shape leaves its statement unreadable: a review. Before that, spans POSITIVELY classified as not temporal, each by a stated non-temporal context (benign: each class with its note - frequencies, telephone numbers, numbers with units, flight levels, route altitudes, altitudes and minima after their keyword, FAA take-off minima, declared distances, bearings, radials and sectors, designators, AIP pages, aircraft types and registrations, NOTAM and document numbers after their keyword, obstruction and permission case numbers, a document's own date, the verb MAY, the sun, marking and lighting by day or night, notice, permission and restoration lead times, contact-office hours, identifiers, positions, magnetic variation epochs, event years, observation times) are masked. A benign span never holds a clock-like range (benignNeverHolds) unless its class states allowClockRange, it never cuts a clock-like shape (benignNeverCuts: it may hold a whole one, as 'TORA 2100' does, never part of one), and it is never one side of a range: it is refused when a range connector joins it to temporal content left unmasked (rangeAbutment). A duration is benign ONLY in an explicit notice, permission or restoration context (PPR 48 HOURS, 24 HR PN, RE-OPN WI 2 HR, MAX RESTORATION TIME 04HRS, FPLS AT LEAST 3 HR BFR THE EOBT, NOTIFY ATC 24 HR IN ADVANCE); a duration attached to the restriction itself (CLSD FOR 2 HR, FOR MAX 2 HOURS, FOR A PERIOD OF 2 HOURS, DURING THE LAST 2 HOURS, WI 2 HR alone) is temporal content: a review, never a start.

Every temporal token must lie in a statement (statement): a maximal run of grammar vocabulary - clocks (with UTC or Z), day numbers, months, years, dates, weekdays, DLY, H24, UFN, PERM - joined by connectives (FROM, TO, UNTIL, THRU, THROUGH, UP TO, BTN/BETWEEN .. AND, ON, EVERY, EV, DURING, HR, THE HOURS OF, OPR HR, HR OF OPERATION, WITH EFFECT FROM, EFFECTIVE, UTC ...). A temporal token outside every statement is a review: there is no path from unmatched text to 'no schedule'. A statement is read whole or it is a review: after its trailing connectives are dropped, an exception, a negation or a local time (negations) makes it unreadable; dates are normalised (prepare: '27TH OF APR', 'AUGUST 16, 2026', ISO dates, BTN date AND date, 'CHANGED TO H24'); calendar periods with a year are read first (periodRange, periodSingle; a start preposition (startPrepositions) gives [date, open), an end preposition (endPrepositions) gives (open, date], ON or none a single day; a start with no time is the start of its day, an end with no time the end of its day; a start with no month or year takes the end's); the rest is rewritten into Item D syntax (rewrite) and read by the Item D grammar, days and hours bound together in either order ('SUN 1800-2000', '1800-2000 ON SUN', 'BTN 1700UTC TO 2200UTC EV SUN AND WED'). Bare numbers, UFN or PERM left alone (ignorable) read as nothing; any other leftover connective (fatal: a one-sided clock such as 'WEF 1800', 'AT 1800', 'UNTIL 1800') and any statement whose temporal content yields neither a period nor a schedule are a review. The free text reads as 'no schedule' only when it holds no temporal content of any shape.

Accounting. A statement holding periods only is accounted for when every period contains the whole B/C validity: a start (WEF, FROM, EFFECTIVE ...) at or before B, an end (UNTIL, TIL, TO ...) at or after C. A start after B - inside the validity or after C - or an end before C - inside it or before B - contradicts the validity and is a review (QA506-02); with an open end (UFN, PERM) an end date always narrows it. A statement holding a schedule must be proven equal, ON ITS OWN - never pooled with other statements, never by day parts or hours checked separately (QA506-03) - to the accepted Item D, or with no Item D to the whole validity (H24): by the same canonical rule set (each day part with its merged hours; all seven weekdays are daily), or by the same occurrences over the whole bounded validity (at most equivalenceEnumerationMaxDays days); a period in the statement clips its occurrences, and a clipped statement needs the bounded proof. An open-ended or longer validity with no structural equality is a review. With no readable validity, every temporal statement is a review. Hours alone ('BTN 0800-1000') are every day; days alone ('ACT MON-FRI') are those whole days.

QA514 (every digit accounted for). After the benign spans are masked, EVERY digit left (accountedResidue) is accounted for exactly as a temporal token is: it must lie in a statement the grammar reads whole and that is proven against Item D or B/C, else a review - there is no path to 'no schedule' while any digit is unaccounted for; the free text reads as 'no schedule' only when, masked, it holds no digit and no temporal content. Shape detection feeds the grammar; it is not the gate. A time in number words (FROM EIGHT TO TEN, TWO H) is temporal content (numberWordTime); a statement never starts right after a sign glued to its value (UNTIL +24 HR). Benign masks are governed by syntax (benignGovernance): a span that is the object of a temporal connective (DURING, OUTSIDE, UNTIL, TILL, TIL, FROM, BEFORE, AFTER, BTN/BETWEEN, AT, BY, WEF, TO, THRU, SINCE - TO, FROM and BY after an amendment verb or UP/SUBJECT take a value) and begins with a digit or a time word is never masked unless it is self-evidently not a time (a unit of length, height, speed, mass, angle or proportion - never a frequency, never minutes or seconds -, a flight level, a position, an approach-minimum pair, a CFR title, a DME distance, the sun as a light source): 'CLSD UNTIL 121.9' is a review; and DURING, DRG, OUTSIDE, SINCE and WEF only ever take a period, so whatever follows them and holds a digit is never masked unless self-evident ('CLSD DRG PHASE 2'). An office's hours (contactHours) are benign only when a contact verb governs them - the nearest verb before them in their sentence is a contact or communication verb, or they open their sentence and the next verb is one - and only the hours phrase is masked (maskGroup): 'CLSD DURING THE OFFICE HOURS OF THE CAA' is a review, 'CLSD. CONTACT CAA DURING NORMAL OFFICE HOURS' is not. Genuine non-time numbers are benign by what governs them: a label of the noun before it (TERMINAL 7, ALERT LVL 2, YUKON 1-5), a count of the noun after it (3 BOATS), a list or section label before a word, a letter-led designator (Q907, RWY13R, LEMOD-N644-DOBAT), a runway end, a location identifier, a visibility after VIS, a FICON code, a DME distance; each states holdsNoTemporal (it never holds a temporal token of the unmasked text), and a count or list label never follows a restriction verb directly. A class that states maskGroup masks only that group of its match.

Grammar, after upper-casing, folding dashes, DAILY->DLY, dropping EVERY/EV/AND, dropping UTC/Z after a time and closing spaces around '-': date parts and time ranges alternate; a date token after a time closes an entry; ',' ';' ':' only separate. A date part is DLY, weekdays (MON-FRI ranges allowed), month days (AUG 12 14 15, AUG 01-05), or a cross-month range (JUL 20-SEP 30). Day numbers with no month take the latest month named earlier in the field, else the validity month when B and C are in one month, else a timing review. Every day must exist: a day past its month's length, or 29 FEB when no leap year falls within the validity, is a timing review. An entry with no date part is daily only when it is the first entry. Times are HHMM-HHMM with HH 00-23 and MM 00-59 (an end before the start crosses midnight; an end equal to the start, such as 1800-1800, is a timing review: no LIDO or ICAO convention for a zero-length range is held here, so it is neither read as 24 hours nor as nothing) or H24. Anything else is a timing review.
Occurrences are clipped to the validity.

Validity not overlapping the window: outside_window (outsideBy validity), decided before any source or schedule review - schedule text that cannot be read cannot put a notice in force outside its own validity; the state is the validity's relation to the reference.

review: the validity could not be read (absent or unreadable start or end), or it overlaps the window and the source record or the schedule could not be read; state unknown_at_reference, no minutes, no reference interval.

With a schedule: occurrences overlapping the window make it affecting; the state is the occurrence covering the reference, else the next one after it, else the last one before it. With none in the window: outside_window, and the state is read from every occurrence searched (validity, at most lookbackDays before the window, and openEndSearchDays after it for an open end).
Without a schedule: affecting; the state is the validity's relation to the reference.
No reference instant: state unknown_at_reference with the status above.
minutesDelta: 0 when active, minutes to the start when it begins after, minutes since the end when it ended before.

reviewReasons.validity: The LIDO VALID range could not be read; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.reviewLanguage: Schedule uses daylight, exception, or holiday rules that are not evaluated; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.freeText: The LIDO record contains schedule language inside free text; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.freeTextConflict: The LIDO record states schedule hours in its free text that its Item D does not account for; the timing is unresolved.

rules: A notice printing dated runway-closure regimes (WSSS SX120/25) is decided per runway: each regime with an occurrence on the reference day, or the previous evening's occurrence still running at the reference, yields that runway's state; the notice itself stays a timing review when other schedule language remains.

This is ODSS's 19 Sep 2026 runway_closure_schedule rule; the dashboard chart now draws the same per-runway state the PDF map and PDF text publish. A regime whose start equals its end is not read (no runway state from it; the notice stays a timing review), as an invalid clock is not.
runwayClosureRegimes.flags: case-insensitive, read against the item text upper-cased with whitespace collapsed
